A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CSM research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-C are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original CSM calibration experiments, OOD detection results, ablations, and appendix evaluations on additional architectures and long-tailed datasets.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds ImageNet evaluations, further ablations, test-time integrations, augmentation-count results, and training-time estimates.

M1.justification: The core diffusion sampling, CLIP-based reannotation, and combined CE/L2 training objective remain unchanged. v2 additionally evaluates optional CSM+TTA and CSM+ProCal inference pipelines in Table 7, providing limited procedural extensions rather than redesigning CSM.

E1.justification: v2 adds ImageNet classification and calibration evaluations in Tables 3-4, substantially extending evaluation scale beyond the existing CIFAR and Tiny-ImageNet benchmarks. OOD scenarios and CIFAR long-tailed evaluations were already present in v1 and are retained.

E2.justification: CALS appears as an additional evaluated comparator in the new ImageNet tables. Table 7 also compares CSM against its TTA and ProCal combinations. Comparator membership in the retained benchmark, OOD, and long-tailed comparisons is unchanged; extending existing baselines to ImageNet does not itself add baseline methods.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce Swin-Transformer-V2, the proximity-informed PIECE metric, test-time calibration combinations, and an explicit Naug=1,2,3 sweep. Previously stated splits, training schedules, augmentation defaults, and EQ-DATA protocol remain unchanged. Detailed ImageNet and test-time integration settings are not supplied.

E4.justification: v2 adds controls using vanilla CLIP labels and one-hot diffusion augmentations, testing the roles of reannotation and soft labels. It also adds test-time complementarity, augmentations-per-training-sample, and training-cost analyses. These substantially broaden diagnostic evidence. Scaling-factor sensitivity already appeared in v1 Appendix C and is merely relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or run-to-run error bars. The added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: The original benchmark, OOD, architecture, and long-tailed scores are retained. New ImageNet results report CSM accuracy/ECE of 79.87/1.32 with ResNet-50 and 81.08/1.49 with Swin-Transformer-V2, alongside new ablation, integration, augmentation-count, and timing results. Findings are mixed: both Table 7 integrations worsen ECE, and CIFAR-100 ECE rises from 1.29 to 1.74 when Naug increases from two to three.

T1.justification: The confidence-balanced loss definition, propositions, reannotation derivation, and Appendix A proofs are unchanged after matching equation numbers. v2 turns an existing inline diffusion-distribution expression into numbered Equation (5) and adds explanatory prose, without introducing new mathematics.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain semantic mixing, calibrated reannotation, and balanced L2 learning for improved calibration. The abstract retains the same scientific claims. The revised conclusion's baseline framing and additional supporting experiments do not materially redefine those contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations attributing vanilla CLIP-label failure to noisy all-class annotations and weak calibration from one-hot augmentations to missing soft-label information. It also discusses augmentation/compute tradeoffs and interprets test-time integration gains as evidence of robustness, although Table 7 shows metric-dependent benefits rather than uniform improvement.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds estimated training times, explicitly states classifier training on a single RTX A4000, and explains that generated samples can be reused across model, objective, and annotation changes. v1 already disclosed A4000 generation costs. The repository link target is unchanged, and the new ImageNet and integration experiments receive little implementation detail.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hekler et al. (2023) on test-time augmentation/calibration and Xiong et al. (2023) on proximity-informed calibration, positioning CSM relative to these approaches. Other reference changes largely update publication metadata or formatting for works already cited.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording and explanatory edits, revises the conclusion, adds acknowledgements, corrects affiliation text, and changes the corresponding author. It moves the scaling-factor discussion from Appendix C into Section 4.2 while preserving the overall narrative and section structure.

P2.justification: Experimental presentation expands with ImageNet, integration, augmentation-count, and timing tables, plus a regrouped and enlarged ablation table. v1 Figure 6 is split between v2 Figures 6 and 7, moving the scaling panels into the main text; existing sample and reliability figures are reordered. Table 6 also introduces a duplicated post-temperature ECE column heading.

improvement.justification: The added CLIP-label and one-hot augmentation controls strengthen support for CSM's design, while ImageNet results and explicit timing comparisons broaden its empirical assessment. These gains are limited by sparse documentation of the new experimental settings and overly positive interpretations of mixed results, especially Table 7's worsened ECE and Table 11's nonmonotonic CIFAR-100 trend.
